prompt:
Create realistic, production-quality UI design with clear hierarchy, strong typography, intentional imagery, and purposeful spacing. Use case: logo-brand and desktop UI visual exploration. Product: Token Overflow, a public debugging evidence library. This is an IN-SITU FULL IDENTITY SYSTEM exploration, not a brand guide, slide, moodboard, giant wordmark artwork or marketing landing page. Output ONE focused full desktop workspace at 1440 x 1024, naturally composed, no collage of alternatives. Current date anchor: 2026-10-30; avoid gratuitous dates/clocks.

Audience: a developer who is stuck and wants a relevant check or a clear reason a change does not apply. The very first impression must feel like opening a small useful program on an old Windows PC. The founder explicitly rejected ALL previous Relay, Proof Tab and Open Loop marks AND the entire wordy AI-ish warm-paper brand-guide design language. Do not recycle corner frames, black/lavender abstract brackets, giant monospaced logos, essay cards, manifestos, generic SaaS dashboards, or modern startup-brand moodboards. New identity belongs naturally in a title bar, application icon and one taskbar item, not a giant hero. Show personality through original icon/art direction, typography, crisp control geometry, tactile chrome, surface/color roles, and human perception of a useful familiar workspace.

References attached in this order: 1-3 are actually inspected public Mobbin Logo gallery captures (https://mobbin.com/explore/web/ui-elements/logo), informing variety, small symbol+wordmark relationships and in-app scale; do NOT copy any pictured trademark, letters or geometry. 4 is the actual PostHog live capture: product-as-desktop metaphor, not its many links, cards, mascot or brand. 5 is the actual current product capture with honest empty corpus, grounding the search→finding→change→check purpose only, NOT a layout to reproduce; do not present its sample as genuine community contribution. TypeSafe and the prior Quiet Desktop sketch were also inspected but are NOT attached because the image tool accepts at most five references. No original Windows screenshot is attached; era cues below are described, not a pixel clone. No Microsoft/Windows/competitor logos, copied wallpaper, copied OS icon files, copyrighted character or affiliation claim.

Focus a primary search and one selected finding. At most two other action labels: "Share finding" and "Connect agent". Keep the window human-sized, readable at 14-16px equivalent; about 100-135 visible words maximum including code. One primary Search action. No fake community stats, reputation, accepted-answer badge, trophies, marketing, tutorial, explanatory essays, onboarding checklist, analytics, AI chat, File/Edit/View menus with invented features, Settings, Teams, History or other product scope. A narrow bottom taskbar is part of this explicitly requested visual desktop exploration; it is not a claim those OS actions are implemented.

Use this compact realistic content, visibly marked "Illustrative example" and "Contributor-reported"; it is conceptual, not a test or genuine community data. Search text: "decimal parsing". Finding title: "Decimals truncated during parsing". Relevant versions: "Node.js 24.0.0 · Linux: unknown". Small code/reproduction: `parseInt("1.5")`. Proposed change: `parseInt(input) → Number(input)`. Same check: `node example.mjs --input 1.5`. Expected: `1.5`. Before: `1`. After: `1.5`. Preserve at least two very compact condition-scoped result lines, not only green success: "Worked · input 1.5" and "Failed · input 1,5 → NaN". Neither is a global truth. Use short precise labels, not long teaching prose. Keep evidence selectable-looking plain type, no rendered screenshot inside screenshot. No whole session. A neutral small "Unknown" remains visible for the OS version. Do not invent a causal claim about ElevenLabs.

Use spacing/grouping/alignment first and thin separators. Chrome borders are appropriate to the requested contained desktop app, but do not stack cards within cards. The main evidence document should read as one working surface. No enormous empty whitespace or giant brand heading. No fake decorative window controls as an implementation requirement: this is a visual exploration only. Do not clip content, crop controls, stretch or warp. No device bezel/monitor photograph. Exact visible product text "tokenoverflow" or "Token Overflow". Let the identity, workspace, icon and working hierarchy carry the feel.

Direction name (internal only; do not print): Patch Pocket. Material visual system: approachable EARLY-2000s XP-ERA SMALL DESKTOP PROGRAM. It must look distinctly different from a Windows Classic teal/silver workbench: luminous cornflower/cobalt blue compact title bar with a subtle rounded upper edge, warm ivory toolbar, very pale blue workspace, a soft original sky-blue desktop background (NO Bliss hills/clouds/Windows art). Crisp small Verdana/Tahoma-like UI, generously readable 14-16px equivalent, no heavy oversize headline/mono brand. ORIGINAL brand identity: a tiny cheerful amber/gold THREE-DIMENSIONAL PIXEL-STYLE PROGRAM ICON of a small overflowing in-tray with one red slip, clean immediately recognizable silhouette, NOT a Microsoft folder/icon, document-tab frame, brackets, lavender corner shape, paperclip or competitor mark. Beside it, a compact friendly blue lowercase 'tokenoverflow' wordmark in a slightly sturdy humanist sans. Amber program icon repeats at 24px on the taskbar, with a tiny red active-state accent. Blue/ivory/amber/red should belong together as one identity family.

Composition: one compact large app window, about 90% of frame with a modest visible sky-blue desktop margin. Top actual search field+Search button. One narrow horizontal results band showing ONLY the selected illustrative finding (do not invent a six-row dataset). Below, a wide white document with the finding title, compact Node/Linux strip and a generous useful side-by-side arrangement: left minimal example and proposed exact change; right same command, Expected1.5 and clearly aligned Before1/After1.5. At bottom two one-line Worked and Failed conditions. The whole screen must feel simpler than a modern dashboard: no sidebar cards or extra navigation tree, no hero, no teaching prose, no tiny menu words. Keep 'Illustrative example · Contributor-reported' in one small neutral status line. Preserve enough empty breathing room, but this is a practical desktop with a useful finding already open, not a brand presentation.

Sparse application chrome and a minimal blue bottom taskbar with ONE active Token Overflow item; no Microsoft Start logo, branded Windows controls or unrelated program/system tray icons. Original in-tray icon should be readable at small size and match tiny utility icon treatment. A tactile search button may carry a restrained amber focus/default edge. Gentle era-accurate highlights only, no plastic bubbles everywhere. Avoid a collage, loud marketing colors or whimsical mascot. No invented reports, duplicate titles, paragraphs explaining why to trust evidence, clock, date or OS version string. Show the exact Expected label and both scoped results.
